tail:
Review written to `research/frontier-14-alpha-b-step3-scaffold-review.md`. Only that file and `scratchpad/alpha-b/` (my closure-checking script) were created — no Beta artifact, `items/`, `library/` or `plan-spec.json` was touched. No permission prompt was raised, and there is no blocker.

## Verdicts

| pair | verdict |
|---|---|
| `triangularisation-and-jordan-canonical-form` | **sufficient** |
| `quadratic-residues-and-the-legendre-symbol` | **sufficient** |
| `reflective-subcategories-and-the-adjoint-functor-theorems` | **insufficient** — B6-1 |

**No split on any pair.** Batch 6 is 43 items (44 with B6-1) against a 60 ceiling; the item list freezes at step 4, so authoring cannot push it over.

## The three things the dispatch asked about

**Batch 4 does not ship existence without uniqueness.** `thm-jordan-form-uniqueness-from-ranks-of-powers` is a separate theorem, the title carries "up to block order", and I checked all four block-count formulas — correct, endpoints included. The MOD-5 leaf witness is on the B page with $J_2(\lambda)^{\oplus 2}$ against $J_2(\lambda)\oplus J_1(\lambda)^{\oplus 2}$; ranks 2 and 1 separate them, and nothing depends on it. The Beta also caught a genuinely false witness in the design's own `FS.` list (geometric multiplicity two versus three) and its replacement is right.

**Batch 5's substitution holds.** The published binomial-congruence items need $n$ to admit a primitive root, $\gcd(a,n)=1$, and $\varphi(p)=p-1$ — and all three side conditions are separately cited at every one of the five uses. No hypothesis is hidden. The floor-free second-supplement replacement closes: I worked the four cases $p=8q+r$ and the counts $2q, 2q{+}1, 2q{+}1, 2q{+}2$ match the parity of $(p^2-1)/8$.

**Batch 6's §6 repair closes** — I worked all four Leinster steps; fullness and local smallness are both load-bearing and both stated. But the Beta raised a *different* blocker, and it is real: MA-2's SAFT with continuity alone cannot be derived. I confirmed it from Riehl's own text (her proof asserts the comma category "has intersections of subobjects created by this functor", which continuity only supplies for small diagrams) and from Mac Lane §V.8, whose Theorem 2 adds "and all pullbacks of families of monics" and uses it at exactly that point. The Beta's two-branch scaffold is what Mac Lane proves. **MA-2 item 26 needs amending, not reverting.**

## What makes batch 6 insufficient

Riehl Example 4.5.13(ii) — commutative rings reflective in rings — was declined `out-of-scope` because "neither [the commutator ideal nor its quotient universal property] is developed by this pair". Both are published and inside this page's declared closure, along with `prop-rings-and-homomorphisms-form-category-ring`. The proof is four lines. Add `thm-commutative-rings-are-reflective-in-rings` to the A page beside its two structural twins.

Also B6-2: two items cite `prop-preorders-as-categories-and-monotone-maps-as-functors` — whose `def-preorder` is on a **set** — to license $\mathbf{Ord}^{op}$ and a proper-class ordinal preorder, where properness is the entire point. That is the §A1 restatement class in the one place it bites.

## Source checks

I built a pypdf venv and extracted rather than relaying status codes. Confirmed: Treil's rank-difference typo is real (p. 281 gives $\dim\ker A^k-\dim\ker A^{k+1}$, which is non-positive); Hackman's harvest is faithful and **NT-2's Hackman locators are the wrong ones**; Riehl's reflection material has moved to §4.5, as the Beta says; Mac Lane recovered from Wayback, not re-sourced. Two locator problems found: Mascot's cited range pp. 8–9 does not contain the example it is cited for (it is p. 10), and two named Mascot results inside that range went unenumerated — one of which is exactly the count theorem that currently has no harvest row.

I did not exhaustively verify the Axler and Hoffman–Kunze headings (124 rows); twenty Axler result numbers were spot-checked and all matched, but Hoffman–Kunze is the range I would sample next.
